result:
I graded `submissions/s2.json` and wrote the grades to `grades/0001-s2.json`. Riley got 3 items correct, 2 partial and 1 wrong.

| Item | Verdict | Note |
|---|---|---|
| q1 | correct | The loop is what makes a system an agent. |
| q2 | correct | The model only writes a tool request, and the program runs the tool. |
| q3 | wrong (M6) | Riley picked "it will eventually fix the bug". An agent needs a stopping condition such as a step limit. |
| q4 | partial (M4) | The answer of 4 is right, but the reasoning says the model runs the tools itself. |
| q5 | correct | Riley gave both parts: the result goes back as the next input, and the model uses it to choose its next step. |
| q6 | partial | Riley said the model picks tools by name only. The model reads the whole description: name, purpose and parameters. |

Riley slipped on "the model requests, the program runs" in q4 after getting it right in q2. The other gaps are stopping conditions, which matter for the budget, and tool descriptions.

I also added `learning-records/0003-quiz-0001-retake-gaps.md` and updated `NOTES.md` with the open misconceptions. `s1` is still ungraded.

**Next step:** Riley should reread the stopping-condition and tool-description parts of the agent-loop lesson. Then Riley should write a full description for the `check_calendar` tool, with a purpose and each parameter. After that, we can move on to context and memory.
